name: Ares Management Corporation
moat_justification: Scaled private-credit-led alternative manager with a durable, diversified fee base (FRE +20% YoY in Q2 2026 on $671.3B AUM / $409.9B fee-paying AUM, record $36.4B raised in the quarter) and through-cycle fundraising - capped at moderate-strong because the product is competitively allocated risk capital: LPs re-bid every vintage among Blackstone/Apollo/KKR/Brookfield/Blue Owl, direct-lending spreads have compressed, earnings are geared to the private-credit cycle, growth has been partly acquired (GCP, BlueCove), and the share count creeps ~3.5%/yr. A 6 gives CAP 9.8 years.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 3.5%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low

WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.4x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Scaled private-credit-led alt manager, moat 6/10 - engine-standardized Tier B (15.95% weighted IRR, IV@15% $122.19) softened to C because the OCF base capitalizes consolidated-fund flows; on TTM after-tax realized earnings of $5.17/share it clears 15% only at ~$84 (~$67 with a margin of safety).
tier_override_reason: SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: the standardized engine base capitalizes consolidated-fund OCF (NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE is structural in 2023, 2024 and 2025, and ttm.py's consolidated-OCF TTM base collapses to $0.4157/share on fund timing), so tier-by-numbers B overstates the manager's distributable owner's earnings; on the manager's realized-earnings definition the weighted IRR is in the low teens (2026-10-13 v4 run: 11.9%, IV@15% $84.17 at $118.15). Softened one notch to C, confidence low - same treatment as ACGL/HIG.
moat_for: Scale and origination in private credit - one of the largest direct-lending platforms globally, inside a $671.3B AUM / $409.9B fee-paying platform
Durability of the fee base - long-dated/perpetual capital share, AUM not yet paying fees as a visible pipeline, FRE +20% YoY in Q2 2026
Diversification and distribution - Credit, Real Assets, Private Equity and Secondaries across institutional, wealth and insurance channels
Through-cycle fundraising record - record $36.4B raised in Q2 2026, $170.0B available capital
moat_against: No structural pricing power - LPs allocate each vintage competitively among Blackstone, Apollo, KKR, Brookfield, Blue Owl and Ares, and direct-lending spreads have compressed
Earnings geared to the private-credit cycle - a default/non-accrual wave hits carried interest, marks, fundraising and the insurance book at once
Growth partly bought, not only earned - GCP International (2025, roughly doubled Real Assets AUM) and BlueCove (Feb 2026); integration and contingent-consideration risk
Regulatory/reputational overhang on private credit and affiliated insurance (Aspida), plus partner-economics dilution - share count growing 3.5%/yr
